summary.text: Josh Shapiro is the incumbent Governor of Pennsylvania, seeking a second term with running mate Austin Davis. He previously served as Attorney General (2017–2023), a Montgomery County commissioner and a state representative. In November 2025 he signed a $50.1 billion budget, approved after a budget impasse of more than four months.

paragraphs.text: Shapiro grew up in Pennsylvania; according to the governor's office, his father is a pediatrician who served in the Navy and his mother is a retired educator.
He studied political science at the University of Rochester, graduating in 1995, and received a law degree from Georgetown University Law Center in 2002.
Before holding office he worked as a congressional staffer, including as chief of staff to U.S. Rep. Joe Hoeffel, and as an attorney.
Shapiro was elected to the Pennsylvania House of Representatives in 2004 and represented the 153rd District from 2005.
In 2011 he was elected to the Montgomery County Board of Commissioners, serving as its chair until 2017.
Shapiro won the Democratic primary for attorney general in April 2016 and defeated Republican state Sen. John Rafferty Jr. that November; he took office in January 2017 and was re-elected in 2020.
In 2022 he was elected governor, defeating Republican Doug Mastriano, and was sworn in in January 2023.
The governor's office highlights, among his actions in office, a state digital services team called CODE PA and the reopening of I-95 in 12 days after a portion of the highway collapsed.
He is married to Lori Shapiro, and they have four children.
